newsitem.title: USA: UAL Corp's United unveils new ad campaign.
newsitem.headline: UAL Corp's United unveils new ad campaign.

text.p: UAL Corp's United Airlines said Thursday it launched its new $125 million advertising called "Rising", based on a commitment to improve customer service.

"Rising is both our new slogan and a watchword," United chairman and chief executive Gerald Greenwald said in a statement. "It tells our customers that we are working hard to improve our products and services to meet their needs."
In launching the new campaign, United said it is temporarily retiring its well-known "Friendly Skies" slogan.
United said the new U.S. ads began running Thursday in print and on television and radio. The international spots will begin in September during peak overseas travel periods.
The campaign was developed by United and its two advertising agencies, Fallon-McElligott of Minneapolis and Young & Rubicam of New York.

The new campaign came of a study of domestic and international air travelers, which showed the U.S. airline industry as a whole has consistently failed to meet its customers' expectations, the company said.
"It would be disingenuous of me to say we weren't already aware of the fact that air travelers were unhappy," Greenwald said. "What shocked us was the depth of the dissatisfaction we uncovered."
